changes.before: Implement cleanTitle(title). Match the worked contract and the changed-input checks without modifying the supplied input values.
changes.after: Remove spaces at a title's edges while keeping the text inside unchanged.

before: A title may have accidental spaces at its edges. Normalization should follow a stated rule instead of silently rewriting meaningful internal spacing.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.
trim() returns a new string with surrounding whitespace removed. It does not change the original string. The type guard prevents calling a string method on a number.

Read the function call cleanTitle("  Moon notes  ") from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, cleanTitle runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
What happens to the two spaces inside " A  B "? Only surrounding whitespace is removed by this rule. The internal text stays unchanged.
after: A title may have extra spaces before or after it. trim() removes surrounding whitespace, such as spaces and line breaks. It keeps the spacing inside the title.
Check typeof title === "string" before calling trim(). This prevents a text operation from being called on a number or another kind of value.
trim() returns new text. It does not edit the original string. Repeated spaces between words also remain, because this rule only cleans the edges.
After trimming, check that the result's length is greater than zero. Empty or whitespace-only text should return null. A non-text input should also return null.
Complete cleanTitle(title). Return trimmed, nonempty text when the input is a string. Return null otherwise. Do not change spacing inside the title.
